importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in PEB contracting services — market is served by regional turnkey contractors and erection subcontractors; buyers search by capability, track record, and geography, not contractor brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: PEB construction is a high-value, project-based service where the seller IS the product — buyers evaluate contractor credentials, past project portfolio, technical capability, and financial standing before any other signal. An unknown contractor with the right specs is still unusable for a crore-plus project.

Service type (turnkey vs erection-only vs design-build), structure type, and material grade are primary shortlisting gates — a buyer seeking a turnkey industrial warehouse contractor will not engage with a fabrication-only or civil-only listing regardless of price or company credentials.

Completed project photos serve as the portfolio proxy — buyers use images to verify the contractor has built structures of comparable scale, type, and quality. A listing with no project photos signals an inexperienced or unverifiable contractor, causing immediate skip in a high-stakes procurement.

Every PEB project is uniquely scoped and quoted as a lump-sum or per-sq-ft estimate; no fixed list price exists. Indicative pricing helps buyers perform a budget sanity check but final price is always negotiated after site visit and detailed scope definition.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Secondary units exist — per sq ft for shed construction benchmarking, per MT for erection-only contracts — but unit is always clarified during project scoping, not at listing-scan stage. No buyer confusion arises from unit absence on the listing tile.
importance_ranking.reason: Project-based pricing means no per-unit price is displayed; unit ambiguity cannot arise at the listing level and is resolved during project scoping conversations.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what the contractor actually delivers — Turnkey Project, Erection Only, Design and Build, or Fabrication Only are non-interchangeable service scopes with fundamentally different project values, team requirements, and buyer eligibility; a buyer cannot substitute one for another.

Defines the physical output being constructed — Industrial Shed, Warehouse, Cold Storage, Multi Storey, Mezzanine Floor — each requires different engineering, load calculations, and compliance standards, driving significant variation in project cost and contractor specialisation.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Clear span width is the primary structural design driver for PEB — it determines column-free interior space, primary frame sizing, and steel tonnage, making it the single most buyer-relevant dimensional spec for warehouse and industrial shed procurement.

Institutional and large industrial buyers shortlist contractors by their proven execution scale — a contractor who has only built 500 MT structures cannot be shortlisted for a 5,000 MT project, making capacity a primary qualification gate.

Whether civil foundation works (RCC footings, anchor bolt setting, grade slab) are included in scope is a critical contract boundary that determines which sub-contractors a buyer must separately engage and significantly affects total project cost.
